analysis:
The only change in docs/architecture/inference.md is documentation: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and the `stop` row of the request-parameter table (line 2126). The row now explains how stop-sequence matching is scoped. GPT-OSS uses the Harmony `final` scope. Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans per request (`ReasoningStopScope`). The native block engine matches the whole output with no scope. The supplied units are base-side excerpts from lines 4003-4494 of the file. They contain none of the changed lines, so the review is only of unchanged surrounding text. That text describes GLM and Qwen tensor parallel, cluster KV precision and SSD prefix records. It also contains the existing sealed-sum, authenticated-record, prefix-scope and fail-closed agreement behaviour. The PR does not alter any of it.

The change is a docs-only edit, so no code, keys, attestation, encryption, prefix-cache (T-041), WebSocket or fan-helper control is modified here. A security-relevant reading of the stop-scope text is possible: a stop string in reasoning or tool-call text could now be ignored, which affects output truncation but not confidentiality or authorization. Whether the code matches this prose (`ReasoningStopScope`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`) is outside the supplied evidence. The docs-only diff does not show a regression. The threat model needs no update, and I did not verify the code behind the claim.
